 High Court Of Andhra Pradesh: At Amaravati

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh: At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Main Case No. W. P. 6212 of 2023
 Proceeding Sheet
Sl. Date Order

J. Trans  W.P.No.6212 of 2023 to I.
 Folde

Learned Assistant Government Pleader for  Land Acquisition takes notice for respondent  No.1, learned Government Pleader for Municipal  Administration and Urban Development takes  notice for respondents 2 and 3, learned  Government Pleader for Revenue takes notice  for respondent No.4, Sri Suresh Kumar Reddy  Kalva, learned Standing Counsel for  Corporations, takes notice for respondent No.5  and Sri P.Muni Reddy, learned Standing  Counsel for TUDA, takes notice for respondent  No.6 and request time for filing counters.
At this stage, the Court is not inclined to  issue notice to respondent No.7 as he is not  a necessary party to the writ petition.

Earlier, the writ petitioner has approached this Court by way of filing W.P. No.1196 of 2023 with a grievance that without acquiring the property of the petitioner as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, that the respondents are making efforts to acquire the said land for widening the road.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: After hearing the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the Corporation in the said writ petition, this Court has disposed of the said writ petition as per the order dated 01-02-2023 with a direction to the 5th respondent therein that if the said land in question is required for public purpose of widening the road as per the master plan, to issue notice to the petitioner under Section 21 of the said Act 2013 and then follow the due process of law in acquiring the said land.

Now, it is the grievance of the writ petitioner that inspite of the aforesaid direction given by this Court in the above writ petition that without issuing any notice as contemplated under Section 21 of the Act 2013 that the respondents in blatant violation of the direction given in the above writ petition have started demolishing the compound wall of the vacant site of the petitioner with JCBs for the purpose of laying road over the said land in the process of widening the road.

1

The petitioner has also produced the photographs showing the land before its demolition of the compound wall and after its demolition of the compound wall which prima facie show that the compound wall was demolished with the help of JCBs.

Sri P.Anand Surendra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the learned Standing Counsel for Corporation Sri Suresh Kumar Reddy Kalva, on written instructions, which are placed on record,
would submit that notices are given to the petitioner to produce all the documents relating to the property.
But it is not stated either in the said written instructions or before this Court at the time of hearing the matter that the said land was acquired as per the procedure prescribed under law.

Therefore, demolishing the compound wall without acquiring the said land formally by following the procedure prescribed under the law is undoubtedly illegal and the said conduct of the respondents in demolishing the compound wall and more particularly in utter violation of the direction given by this Court in the earlier writ petition is most reprehensible in the nature of it.

Therefore, in the said facts and circumstances of the case, there shall be interim direction to the respondents not to proceed with further demolition of the compound wall and not to proceed further in laying any road in the disputed site till the next date of hearing.

CMR, J.
Note:-
Issue C.C. by 15-3-2023.
